contract_plain_english: When multiplying two matrices that may already be inaccurate, the first-order absolute normwise error is split into three additive pieces: fresh multiplication roundoff μ(n)ε||A||||B||, propagation of B's error as ||A||err(B,n), and propagation of A's error as err(A,n)||B||. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: equation (8)).

source_evidence.observation: The rule is introduced for computing C = A·B when A and B already have inherited errors err(A,n) and err(B,n), within a first-order absolute-error analysis.
The paper gives err(C,n) = μ(n)ε||A||·||B|| + ||A||·err(B,n) + err(A,n)·||B||.
The three summands are respectively attributed to matrix multiplication, amplification of B's inherited error by ||A||, and amplification of A's inherited error by ||B||.
The underlying local multiplication guarantee is normwise: ||Ccomp−C|| ≤ μ(n)ε||A||||B|| + O(ε²), with ε machine epsilon and μ(n) a low-degree polynomial.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The contract is the local three-term error-propagation rule used whenever the recursive algorithm multiplies matrices that may themselves be inexact; it does not depend on the order in which the surrounding triangular-inversion products are associated. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: equation (8) and the subsequent note choosing to premultiply T12 first).
binders: n is the size parameter used by μ and each err quantity. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: equation (8)).
A and B are conformable matrices, C = A·B, and A and B may each carry inherited errors from prior computations. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: paragraph before equation (8)).
conclusions: The complete displayed first-order product-error rule is err(C,n) = μ(n)ε||A||||B|| + ||A||err(B,n) + err(A,n)||B||. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: equation (8)).
The first summand is newly introduced local matrix-multiplication error. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: first line of equation (8) and annotation 'from matrix multiplication').
The second summand propagates the inherited error in B and amplifies it by ||A||. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: second line of equation (8)).
The third summand propagates the inherited error in A and amplifies it by ||B||. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: third line of equation (8)).
constants_and_indexing: Each of the three displayed contributions has coefficient 1 apart from the explicitly displayed μ(n)ε factor in the local term. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: equation (8)).
The size argument n is unchanged across err(C,n), err(A,n), and err(B,n). (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: equation (8)).
Propagation is cross-oriented: err(B,n) is multiplied by ||A||, while err(A,n) is multiplied by ||B||. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: second and third lines of equation (8)).
definitions_and_conventions: err(C,n), err(A,n), and err(B,n) are absolute normwise error quantities in this first-order accounting. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: first-order absolute-error paragraph and equation (8)).
μ(n) is the dimension-dependent stability factor belonging to matrix multiplication. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 60, anchor: equation (1) and definition of μ).
The rule separates newly generated local roundoff from propagation of errors already present in each operand. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: annotations in equation (8)).
error_notions: The rule concerns absolute normwise forward error in the computed product, not componentwise error. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: first-order absolute-error paragraph and equation (8)).
It accounts separately for local multiplication error, inherited right-input error, and inherited left-input error. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: all three annotations in equation (8)).
exceptional_values: No assumptions or conclusions concerning overflow, underflow, NaN, infinity, or other exceptional floating-point values are stated with equations (1) or (8). (PDF p. 2, printed p. 60, anchor: equation (1); PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: equation (8)).
higher_order_terms: The rule is explicitly first order and does not display a product err(A,n)err(B,n), ε times an inherited error, or an O(ε²) remainder. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: paragraph before equation (8) and equation (8)).
Equation (1), from which the local multiplication term is inherited, includes +O(ε²). (PDF p. 2, printed p. 60, anchor: equation (1)).
hypotheses: The product C is evaluated under the paper's stable normwise matrix-multiplication model. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 60, anchor: equation (1); PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: equation (8)).
The analysis is first order. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: paragraph before equation (8)).
The two operands have inherited errors denoted err(A,n) and err(B,n). (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: paragraph before equation (8)).
implicit_context: Equation (8) is subsequently applied repeatedly to products in recursive triangular matrix inversion. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: text following equation (8) and displayed recursive bounds).

The surrounding application uses square recursive blocks, but the rule's own introductory sentence only requires a matrix product C = A·B. (PDF p. 7, printed p. 65, anchor: recursive inverse block formula; PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: paragraph before equation (8)).
norms: All three terms use matrix norms: the local term contains ||A||||B||, right-error propagation contains ||A||, and left-error propagation contains ||B||. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: equation (8)).

No specific norm is named in equation (8); the earlier multiplication model permits changing norms with additional dimension-dependent factors. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 60, anchor: paragraph after equation (1); PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: equation (8)).
numerical_model: ε is machine epsilon. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 60, anchor: equation (1) explanatory paragraph).
μ(n) is a low-degree polynomial in n, μ(n) = O(n^c) for some constant c. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 60, anchor: equation (1) explanatory paragraph).
Only the local multiplication term is explicitly proportional to ε; inherited errors are propagated through the other two terms. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: equation (8)).

The local term is μ(n)ε||A||||B||. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: first line of equation (8)).
Right-input error contributes ||A||err(B,n). (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: second line of equation (8)).
Left-input error contributes err(A,n)||B||. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: third line of equation (8)).
The rule is first-order, absolute, and normwise. (PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, anchor: paragraph before equation (8)).
